title: Dynamic interleaved KV strata coordinator for continuous batching across tensor/pipeline parallelism
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a coordinator layer that manages interleaved 'strata' placements of KV shards across GPU memory to reduce fragmentation and improve tail latency for continuous streaming batches in mixed tensor/pipeline parallel topologies.
background: We observe two recurring issues on production workloads with long-lived KV cache and continuous batching: 1) fragmentation of small KV allocations across heterogeneous GPUs (tensor vs pipeline parallel placements) leads to wasted memory and early spills; 2) request-level batching that spans different pipeline stages produces uneven KV load hotspots and causes synchronous stalls during prefetch/eviction. Existing slab/shard designs assume either pure tensor or pure pipeline layouts and rely on static stripe sizes which are suboptimal for streaming chat workloads with variable context lengths.
proposed_solution: Introduce an 'Interleaved KV Strata Coordinator' (IKSC) that: (a) organizes KV memory into logical strata (hot, warm, cold) with adaptive stripe widths per GPU based on topology hints (tensor/pipeline role, local memory pressure, PCIe/NVLink bandwidth), (b) assigns micro-slabs interleaved across GPUs so that single-request KV spans are packed to minimize cross-device fetches while still balancing hot-key concentration, (c) maintains a lightweight distributed directory (per-GPU bloom filter + versioned epoch) for membership checks to avoid synchronous RPCs during generation, (d) exposes eviction/prioritization hooks to the continuous batching scheduler to apply backpressure or prefetch based on in-flight batch signatures.
acceptance_criteria: IKSC design doc approved by runtime and infra leads
Prototype implements micro-slab allocator and strata placement policy for a 4-GPU tensor+pipeline topology (tensor-parallel 2 x pipeline-parallel 2)
End-to-end integration with continuous batching scheduler so that during mixed streaming workloads, tail P99 latency reduces by >= 15% compared to baseline sharding with equal memory budget
Memory fragmentation (measured as sum of free tiny segments < 4MB) decreases by >= 30% under long-lived chat replay tests
No increase in total per-token CPU overhead beyond 8% compared to current allocator at runtime settings used in benchmarks
Automated test suite covers eviction correctness, directory versioning, and failure recovery (GPU disconnect simulation)
implementation_plan: Week 1: Design finalization and API surface for strata coordinator + distributed directory; gather topology hints available from orchestrator (tensor/pipeline roles).
Week 2: Implement local micro-slab allocator and strata metadata on one GPU; unit tests for allocation/eviction semantics.
Week 3: Implement interleaving policy and directory (epoched bloom + per-slab version); add membership check fast-path in runtime generation loop.
Week 4: Integrate with continuous batching scheduler to surface backpressure signals and prefetch intents; add metrics hooks.
Week 5: Multi-GPU integration tests on 4-GPU topology; run long-lived chat replay workloads and compare fragmentation and tail latency.
Week 6: Performance tuning, safety checks (fallback to existing shard protocol), and documentation for config knobs (strata thresholds, stripe sizing heuristic).
Week 7: Canary rollout to dedicated staging cluster; collect telemetry; iterate on eviction heuristics.
Week 8: Merge final changes and prepare runtime-1.22 patch release notes.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Directory false positives/negatives could cause extra fetches or stale reads. Mitigation: use versioned epochs + conservative fallback reads; include periodic reconciliation pass.

Risk: Cross-device interleaving increases PCIe traffic and could worsen latency on bandwidth-constrained topologies. Mitigation: topology-aware stripe widths and prefer local coalescing for hot keys; add per-GPU bandwidth budget cap.
Risk: Complexity in allocator increases CPU overhead. Mitigation: keep membership checks probabilistic and inline fast-path; offload expensive reconciliation to background workers.

Risk: Interaction with existing checkpoint/restore flow. Mitigation: ensure strata metadata is serializable; add migration path that converts old slab maps to strata map during restart with throttled warmup.
Risk: Regression for pure tensor-parallel workloads. Mitigation: detect homogeneous topologies and reduce to existing optimized sharding policy (feature flag).
metrics_and_tests: Primary metrics: generation P50/P95/P99 latency, memory fragmentation ratio, per-GPU memory utilization, PCIe traffic per-second, per-token CPU time
Synthetic tests: variable-length chat replay (5k sessions, mean context 8k, 10% context growth), long-lived KV retention (24 hours) to measure fragmentation
Integration tests: GPU disconnect/reconnect scenario ensuring directory epoch recovery; correctness tests for eviction order and no lost KV entries
A/B experiments: compare IKSC vs baseline shard in staging with production-like load; run for minimum 72 hours to capture tail behavior
Performance budget: overhead at p50 per-token CPU must stay within 8% and network traffic should not exceed 20% increase on target topologies
rollout_plan: Feature behind runtime feature flag (iksc.enabled) default false
Canary 1: Single customer staging cluster (4-GPU) with iksc enabled for non-sensitive workloads
Canary 2: Broader dedicated pool with mixed tensor/pipeline jobs; monitor P99, fragmentation, and PCIe saturation
If metrics stable for 7 days, enable for low-traffic production routes with gradual ramp and quick rollback path
Document migration steps and provide operator runbook for increasing/decreasing strata thresholds
dependencies: infra/networking: telemetry for per-GPU PCIe/NVLink counters
scheduler: exposure of continuous-batching in-flight signatures API
